request.spec:
People have a position in the list. Up and down buttons on the row swap the person with the one
above or below (PERSON_MOVED name=<name> position=<new position, counting from 1>); the top row
cannot move up nor the bottom row down (refused with an error on the row). The list, the rollup lines
and every action that works in list order follow the positions. New people go to the end.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
People have a position in the list. Up and down buttons on the row swap the person with the one
above or below (PERSON_MOVED name=<name> position=<new position, counting from 1>); the top row
cannot move up nor the bottom row down (refused with an error on the row). The list, the rollup lines
and every action that works in list order follow the positions. New people go to the end.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
People now have a position in the list, and each row has up and down buttons. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**What changed**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V58__person_position.sql`, adds a `list_position` column to the person table and to its `hist`/`asof` copies, which "as of a date" views read. Existing people get positions in the order they were added. A new person, including one transferred in from another sheet, goes to the end of the list.
- **Order everywhere:** `PersonRepository.list` now sorts by position. Everything that works in list order already reads people through it, so it all follows the positions: the people list, the rollup lines and snapshots, bulk open/settle/reassign, bulk grade and the CSV export.
- **Moving:** a new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/move`, takes `direction: up|down`. It swaps the person with their neighbour and writes `PERSON_MOVED … name=<name> position=<new position, counting from 1>` to the audit file. Moving the top row up or the bottom row down is refused with an error and nothing is written. Viewers and archived sheets are refused, the same as for other changes.
- **Screen:** a new `features/move/move.slot.tsx` adds the `person-move-up` and `person-move-down` buttons to each row. A refusal shows in the row's `person-error`, which clears on the next action taken on that row.

**Things to know**
- **Retired people count:** positions cover everyone on the sheet, including retired people. With "show retired" off, a hidden retired person can be the one swapped with, so a press may not visibly change the order.
- **Two users moving at once:** a move rewrites every position on the sheet, with no version check. If two people move rows at the same moment, the second move can silently undo the first.

I also updated the code comments that said "in the order they were added" so they now say list order.
